meta.description: Security-lens regression for PR #1934: the 'Agent-initiated file reads' clause exempts secret-bearing files (private keys, .env-style config, token/credential files) from byte persistence. Scripts the compliant shape: the agent reads a synthetic .env-style file with a host tool, then stores only a redacted derived record (variable names, never values) and flags the provenance gap. Asserts the run contains no store carrying file_path or file_content for it: no /store request body carries either field, and the captured mcp_neotoma_store tool_invocation input names neither (and is not truncated, so the absence check saw the whole call). LIMIT, shared with every fixture in this lane: events are replayed hook payloads, so the instruction text never enters this path and the fixture cannot go red if the clause regresses; the unit text-pins in tests/unit/mcp_instruction_doc.test.ts are what fail then. A variant of this fixture that adds file_path to the store goes red on the absence assertions. All paths and values are synthetic placeholders.

payload.prompt: Check /Users/agent/workspace/billing-service/.env and record which external services this project is configured to use.

entities.provenance_gap: secret-bearing file; bytes not stored by design

payload.text: Recorded the billing-service configuration as variable names only (a database, a payments API, and SMTP mail). The .env file holds secrets, so its contents were not stored; the record notes that the original file is intentionally not preserved.
